chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mu'az informed us, saying: Ali ibn Khashram narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Yunus narrated, from Abi Mu'amir, from Sa'id al-Maqbri, from Abu Hurayrah, saying:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table where wine is being drunk; and whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him not enter the bathhouse except with a waistcloth; and whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him not let his wife go out to the bathhouse.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three things a believer should avoid according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a triad of modesty (haya) linking internal faith to external conduct, emphasizing that belief in the Hereafter necessitates vigilance in social and private spheres. The prohibition against wine consumption highlights the avoidance of major sins, while the bathhouse regulations reflect the Shia emphasis on sexual modesty and the protection of family honor within the domestic sphere.
